items.title: Disaster Robotics in the Deep Learning Era]{Disaster Robotics in the Deep Learning Era: A Systematic Review of Platforms, Autonomy, Methods, Datasets, Challenges, and Future Research Directions
items.abstract: Disaster robotics enables responders to sense and act at a disaster site from a safe distance, converting responder risk into an equipment one. The field is increasingly shaped by deep learning and, most recently, by foundation models. However, existing surveys adopt a single perspective or platform class, predate the deep learning era or remain largely narrative. Moreover, none grades every reviewed work on a common validation maturity scale. This paper presents a systematic review of disaster robotics in the deep learning era, restricted to disaster-connected works evaluated on disaster data or in real, replicated or simulated emergency settings. The evolution of the field is traced through successive research phases, from teleoperated platforms to foundation-model interfaces and responder-grounded field autonomy. A multi-criteria taxonomy is formed, covering response tasks, robotic platforms, perception, autonomy, learning strategies, foundation model types, human-robot teaming, coordination, communication and deployment, disaster domains, and validation maturity. Each criterion is analyzed comparatively, with critical insights into the strengths and limitations of its categories under field conditions. Additionally, public datasets and benchmarks are reviewed. Current challenges are also paired with future research directions, from data acquisition and field hardening to verifiable autonomy, responder trust and evaluation. The analysis shows that systems deployed at real incidents still rely predominantly on model-based methods. It also shows that recent research leans increasingly on simulation and benchmark evaluation. Finally, foundation models have entered the field mainly as perception front ends and mission-level planners rather than as embodied policies, without yet reaching a real incident.

items.abstract: Resumen Este trabajo presenta el diseño de un programa de promoción de la salud cardiovascular integrado al SG-SST de ACH Colombia S. A., formulado a partir del diagnóstico de condiciones de salud derivado de los exámenes médicos ocupacionales. La propuesta delimita el problema en torno a factores de riesgo cardiovascular modificables, en particular la inactividad física y el exceso de peso, así como a su interacción con exposiciones ocupacionales relevantes identificadas en el diagnóstico. Con base en una revisión documental de referentes conceptuales, normativos y técnicos, se definen la estructura del programa, sus componentes, líneas de acción e indicadores de seguimiento, dentro de un enfoque preventivo y de mejora continua. El alcance del estudio se limita al diseño técnico de la propuesta, sin incluir su implementación ni la evaluación de su impacto en el corto plazo. Palabras clave: salud cardiovascular; promoción de la salud; SG‑SST; sedentarismo; obesidad; riesgo ergonómico. Abstract This study presents the design of a cardiovascular health promotion program integrated into the Occupational Health and Safety Management System (SG-SST) of ACH Colombia S. A., based on the diagnosis of workers’ health conditions derived from occupational medical examinations. The proposal focuses on modifiable cardiovascular risk factors, particularly physical inactivity and excess body weight, and on their interaction with relevant occupational exposures identified in the diagnosis. Based on a documentary review of conceptual, regulatory, and technical references, the study defines the program structure, components, lines of action, and monitoring indicators to support preventive management and continual improvement. The scope of the study is limited to the technical design of the proposal and does not include implementation or short-term impact assessment. items.title: Divergent Uptake of Apology as Admission or Commitment: Why One Apology Can Be Heard as Several Different Promises
items.abstract: This conceptual paper introduces Divergent Uptake of Apology as Admission or Commitment, a mechanism by which a single apology is understood by different recipients as containing different admissions or commitments. An acknowledgment may be taken as conceding a particular wrong, promising future action, or asking for forgiveness. The expectations formed through these readings can extend beyond what the speaker stated, while the public meaning of the act cannot be reduced to the speaker's private intention. The paper assesses an apology by distinguishing the scope of admission, undertaking, forgiveness, and repair. It asks what the speaker acknowledged, on whose behalf, what was promised or excluded, and what different recipients took the act to settle. A sincere apology may leave an unresolved issue untouched, and an accepted admission does not establish forgiveness or completed repair. Divergent interpretations require evidence of what recipients understood, rather than an assumption that disagreement or dissatisfaction reflects misunderstanding. The discussion places the mechanism alongside J. L. Austin's account of uptake in speech acts and examines two documented cases. After the Netherlands defeated Mexico in the 2014 World Cup, Arjen Robben apologized for diving earlier in the match while maintaining that the winning penalty was legitimate. Published reports assigned his admission to different incidents, with shortening and translation complicating the record. In December 2020, CD Projekt Red apologized for the console release of Cyberpunk 2077 and directed dissatisfied customers toward refund procedures. One reader understood the letter as implying an exception to Sony's normal policy, while another understood that the store retained authority over refunds. The company subsequently confirmed that no special refund arrangement existed at the time of the apology. Part of the Trust, Participation, and Repair series within On Human Modeling, the paper examines who defines what an apology admitted, who may declare repair or forgiveness complete, and what evidence supports competing interpretations. Potential applications in human–AI research include conversational repair, institutional apologies, customer-support systems, and evaluations that distinguish acknowledgment from commitment, forgiveness, and completed remedy.

items.title: Does It Depend on the Split? Frozen Satellite Features vs. Fine-Tuned CNNs for Tree Species Mapping
items.abstract: Self-supervised foundation models are often said to need fewer labels than supervised training. We test this on a forestry task: classifying 20 tree species classes in 0.2 m aerial images from the TreeSatAI dataset. We compare a frozen DINOv3 model pretrained on 493 million satellite images, with only a linear classifier trained on top, against an ImageNet ResNet-50 that is fine-tuned end to end. On the official split, fine-tuning wins clearly (macro F1 0.764 vs. 0.685). However, 28.8% of the official test patches overlap a training or validation patch, and copying the label of the nearest such patch is correct for 83.6% of them. We therefore build a spatial split that holds out whole 2 km squares with a 200 m buffer. On this split the comparison becomes inconclusive (0.648 vs. 0.640, paired 95% CI of the difference [-0.054, 0.016]), and the learning curves of the two models overlap at every label budget from 343 to 33,126 training patches. On the five rarest classes, the frozen model achieves a higher mean F1 (0.566 vs. 0.445), although the confidence interval for this difference includes zero ([-0.05, 0.23]). Diagnostics show that the frozen features mainly miss differences between closely related species, such as the two native oaks. Choosing the input size and layer on validation data (224 px, block 16) raises the frozen model to 0.662 on the spatial split. A comparison that looks decisive on the official split is thus inconclusive under geographically separated evaluation. We release the spatial split and our code.

items.title: Does Learning from Unlabeled Data Help Cancer Diagnosis and Prognosis? Semi-Supervised and Self-Supervised Learning Versus Tabular Foundation Model
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Machine learning for cancer diagnosis and prognosis requires costly patient labels. Semi- and self-supervised methods exploit unlabeled data but are rarely tested against equivalent supervised models. We tested whether unlabeled data help and compared these methods with a tabular foundation model. Methods: Four public breast cancer datasets (WDBC, Mammography, METABRIC, SEER) crossed clinical task (diagnosis, including the detection of microcalcifications on Mammography, or prognosis) with class balance. In five-fold cross-validation with five seeds, 10%, 20%, or 50% of training records were labeled. Self-training (random forest and XGBoost), label spreading, and SCARF self-supervised pretraining were each compared with a matched supervised control; logistic regression and TabPFN v2 were references. Analyses used corrected resampled t-tests with Holm adjustment, Bayesian correlated and hierarchical tests, and power analysis. Results: Of 96 comparisons with matched controls in the Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) and the area under the precision–recall curve (PR-AUC), three were significant, all involving SCARF: two losses on Mammography and one PR-AUC gain on METABRIC that persisted with all labels. The estimated minimum detectable effects at 80% power varied across comparisons, with medians of approximately 0.06 in PR-AUC and 0.09 in MCC; the median absolute observed differences were 0.008 and 0.015, respectively. At the default threshold and 10% labels, label spreading lowered sensitivity on SEER (−0.135) and random-forest self-training on Mammography (−0.122). TabPFN had the highest PR-AUC in all 16 settings. Conclusions: Under the evaluated datasets, methods and settings, no statistically significant additional benefit from unlabeled data beyond shared preprocessing was detected, but the evidence does not establish equivalence; TabPFN achieved the highest PR-AUC in every setting. New methods should be tested against matched controls and tabular foundation models with adequate power.

items.title: DS2Agent: Holistic Device Agents for Accelerated Embedded Board-Level Design
items.abstract: Embedded board-level development demands extensive expertise, from component selection and device characteristics to interface configuration, driver writing, and system composition. Recently, LLM-based agents have shown strong capabilities, raising the prospect of automating board-level design tasks. However, existing agents either target chip-level design or treat datasheets as static text, offering little guidance on whether a specific component should---or even could---be used for a given board-level design. Moreover, without touching real hardware, they hallucinate incorrect details. To fill this gap, we present {\setlength{\fboxsep}{1pt}\href{https://anonymous.4open.science/r/DS2Agent-9FE8/}{\fcolorbox{blue}{white}{DS2Agent}}}, an open-source framework that constructs interactive agents from device datasheets. Each agent comprises three models: a knowledge model supporting retrieval and question answering; a digital-twin model capturing the physical functionality of the device; and an interface model supporting driver development and system integration. To suppress hallucinations, we also allow optional connections to real devices, so that the agent can calibrate its internalized knowledge against the device. We evaluate DS2Agent on ten devices spanning seven functional categories. Compared with the baseline, the DS2Agent-augmented agent improves the question-answering score from 87 to 97 out of 100 while using 44.8\% fewer tokens. For driver generation, it reduces average token usage per device by 72.9\%. For system integration, it reduces total token usage across three FreeRTOS applications by 29.7\%.

items.title: Dynamic Human-Robot Role Allocation through Entropy-Based Monitoring and LLM Reasoning
items.abstract: Role allocation strategies in human-robot collaboration typically assign tasks to both the human and the robot, limiting the user's ability to take initiative. Furthermore, allocation decisions may conflict with the user's intentions, and the rationale behind such allocations may remain unclear, potentially reducing both acceptance and collaboration fluency. The novelty of the proposed framework is that the human is left free to contribute to the task, while the robot is dynamically allocated activities through a cost-driven Behavior Tree architecture according to user-expressed preferences and behavior. Explicit preferences are extracted from natural language instructions using a large language model, whereas human activity is monitored online through a Shannon entropy-based analysis of hand-object interactions. Furthermore, the framework can recognize anomalies in human execution and autonomously trigger corrective robot actions. The approach was validated through a pilot study and a multi-subject experiment involving 14 participants. Results demonstrate the potential of such an allocation strategy for enabling intuitive and engaging collaboration without increasing the perceived workload.

items.title: Early Detection of Ovarian Cancer: Current Strategies and Future Directions
items.abstract: Ovarian cancer (OC) is a major cause of cancer-related mortality among women worldwide, mainly because most cases are diagnosed at advanced stages due to non-specific early symptoms. Although early detection is essential for improving clinical outcomes, accurate and accessible screening remains a major challenge, owing to the non-specific nature of early symptoms, the pronounced histological and molecular heterogeneity of the disease, and the poor performance of conventional screening approaches based on cancer antigen 125 (CA-125), human epididymis protein 4 (HE4) and imaging modalities. This review outlines the major biological and technical challenges in the early diagnosis of OC, briefly summarizes the value and limitations of conventional diagnostic approaches and focuses on current progress in emerging biomarkers, including circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA)/cell-free DNA (cfDNA) alterations, exosomal biomarkers and mesothelin multi-marker combined detection strategies, and novel technologies, such as artificial intelligence, nanotechnology, single-cell sequencing and biosensors for early detection. We also discuss the advantages, current limitations, practical considerations and translational barriers of these approaches. Future advances in OC screening will require the integration of sensitive biomarkers, multimodal detection strategies and more accessible, cost-effective technologies to improve early diagnosis and patient survival.

items.title: ECHO: In-Context Behavior foundation model for Humanoid Whole-Body Control
items.abstract: Humanoid behavior foundation models (BFMs) acquire diverse skills through large-scale motion imitation and massively parallel reinforcement learning, yet broad behavioral capability does not ensure precise execution across physical conditions. Without distinguishing the underlying dynamics, policies may favor conservative compromises over environment-specific precision. We introduce ECHO, an in-context BFM that turns interaction experience into environment-specific control, separating general behavioral capability from dynamics-specific execution. Mixed and Annealed Sampling first establishes a behavior prior in a single pretraining stage by balancing targeted practice with broad motion coverage. Building on this prior, Context Representation and Residual Adaptation learns structured dynamics representations from interaction histories to guide residual corrections to the frozen prior, enabling adaptation without test-time parameter updates. Extensive experiments show that ECHO outperforms all baseline methods across diverse motions and physical conditions. Moreover, deployment on the Unitree G1 demonstrates whole-body teleoperation spanning extreme acrobatics and terrain interaction, alongside payload adaptation in manipulation and whole-body control. Page is available at https://mwondering.github.io/echo-bfm/

items.title: Edge Intelligence in Precision Agriculture: A Multimodal IoT-Driven Framework for Predictive Eustress Management in Medicinal Plants, with Statistically Validated Reinforcement-Learning Control
items.abstract: Medicinal plants grown under water stress are not simply surviving it—many respond to a mild, well-timed drought by producing more of the secondary metabolites that make them valuable, provided the stress never tips into outright damage. Growers call the useful kind eustress and the harmful kind distress, and keeping a crop inside that narrow window is a harder control problem than ordinary irrigation scheduling, especially once a cloud-connected system has to add network latency and tolerate dropped links into the mix. This paper proposes an edge artificial intelligence (AI) and Internet of Things (IoT) framework that pairs a MobileNetV2–LSTM–Transformer fusion design with a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) irrigation agent, keeping the whole decision loop local to the field. The fusion network itself is not trained here; what we test is the control policy alone, in a reproducible simulation of the eustress decision problem. No accuracy metric for the fusion network, no energy measurement and no secondary-metabolite outcome is reported; the stress band and distress threshold are generic modeling choices, and every control result is a property of the simulator. Five independently trained PPO agents were compared against four baselines—no irrigation, a constant dose, a threshold rule, and a carefully tuned PID controller—on 30 shared held-out weather scenarios using paired statistical tests with Holm–Bonferroni correction. The learned policy did not beat the threshold and constant-dose rules on band occupancy (13.7% versus 14.3–15.6%), and the tuned PID controller clearly outperformed it there (32.8%, p < 10−4). PPO reached the lowest distress exposure, only reaching distress 7.4% of the time, compared with 12.4–74.2% for the baselines (p < 10−4), but this is a trade-off of the tested configuration (λ3 = 6), obtained at higher water use (406 L versus 0–259 L) and lower band occupancy than the tuned PID; it is not a general advantage over PID. Pushed into an unseen heatwave, both PPO and PID held onto partial control (61.0% and 72.8% distress) while the remaining baselines essentially collapsed (about 99% distress). A reward-component ablation and a weight sweep trace this behavior back to the distress penalty specifically, with a smaller penalty weight trading some of that distress protection for higher band occupancy. No single controller came out ahead on every measure we tracked.

items.title: Education Management Strategies in Facing the Challenges of the Digital Era
items.abstract: Purpose – This study examines education management strategies for addressing interrelated challenges of digital transformation and develops an integrated interpretation of institutional management priorities in the digital era. Design/methods/approach – A descriptive-qualitative literature review examined relevant national and international scholarly publications, emphasizing research from 2021–2026 alongside selected foundational studies. The sources were organized by recurring institutional challenges and interpreted through thematic comparison and narrative synthesis. Findings – Four interconnected challenges were identified: unequal digital infrastructure and access, limited digital competence, resistance to organizational change, and ethical and data-security risks. Corresponding priorities include inclusive infrastructure planning, continuous professional development, participatory digital leadership, and accountable governance of educational data and artificial intelligence. Addressing these priorities together offers a more coherent managerial response than isolated technology initiatives. Research implications/limitations – The synthesis offers practical considerations for institutional planning and a conceptual basis for future empirical evaluation. As a narrative review, it cannot establish causal effects, determine the relative prevalence of barriers, or compare intervention effectiveness across educational settings. Originality/value – The article connects established digital transformation challenges with complementary management responses, emphasizing the coordination of technological, human, organizational, and ethical dimensions rather than technology adoption alone.

items.title: Educational service quality in higher education: A systematic review and thematic synthesis of qualitative and mixed-methods evidence
items.abstract: This review synthesized qualitative evidence on how students, staff, leaders and employers conceptualize and perceive educational service quality in higher education. Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 statement, a Scopus search of articles published between 2020 and 2026 identified 890 records. After artificial intelligence-assisted title and abstract screening, validated manually on a random sample, and full-text assessment by two authors, 27 qualitative and mixed-methods studies were included. Quality was appraised with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool, and findings were analyzed through thematic synthesis. Seven analytical themes and 22 sub-themes were identified: teaching and academic quality; physical, digital and learning infrastructure; administrative and student support services; employability, practice and personal development; relational and co-created quality; institutional and organizational conditions; and well-being, safety and basic needs. All themes were retained in sensitivity analyses, although support for employability depended largely on weaker studies. Read through a structure–process–outcome lens, the themes distinguish the institutional and basic conditions of the service, its academic, administrative and relational processes, and its expected outcomes. Compared with established instruments, institutional conditions were absent, whereas basic needs, co-creation and labor-market links were insufficiently specified. The findings are limited by a single English-language database search, six unretrieved reports and the interpretive nature of the framework. Quality assurance may benefit from approaches that also consider the conditions under which educational services are produced.

items.title: Effectiveness of an Artificial Intelligence-Based Facial Gesture-Controlled Game in Dysphagia Rehabilitation Following Traumatic Brain Injury
items.abstract: Objectives: To compare AI-based gamified therapy with conventional orofacial physiotherapy in improving swallowing function, therapy compliance, and oral intake among individuals with post-traumatic brain injury dysphagia. Material and Methods: In this pilot randomized controlled trial, 10 participants aged 18–60 years with post-traumatic dysphagia, minimum Rancho Los Amigos Level 5, and Glasgow Coma Scale ≥12 were randomly assigned to AI intervention or conventional therapy groups. Interventions were delivered 5 days/week for 4 weeks. Outcomes included the Dysphagia Outcome and Severity Scale (DOSS), Functional Oral Intake Scale (FOIS), Self-Reported Compliance Scale, and Ryle?s tube-to-oral transition. Non-parametric statistical tests were used. Results: The AI group demonstrated significant improvements in DOSS ( p = 0.004, r = 0.80) and FOIS ( p = 0.039, r = 0.84). Between-group differences were significant for DOSS ( p = 0.011, r = 0.80) and FOIS ( p = 0.017, r = 0.84). Compliance was significantly higher in the AI group ( p = 0.012). Among the three intervention-group participants who were Ryle’s tube dependent at baseline, two (66.7%) transitioned to full oral intake, compared with none of the two tube-dependent participants in the conventional therapy group ( p = 0.30). Conclusion: AI-powered gamified therapy shows promising preliminary benefits in swallowing recovery, therapy compliance, and functional oral intake following traumatic brain injury. Larger randomized controlled trials are warranted.

items.title: Effects of instructional format on knowledge outcomes in risk assessment training: A four-arm quasi-experimental study
items.abstract: Background Risk assessment training is a core component of occupational health and safety (OHS) education, requiring conceptual integration and procedural reasoning. With the increasing use of digital technologies, instructional content is delivered through various formats; however, comparative evidence for conceptually demanding OHS topics remains limited. Objective To compare the effects of four instructional formats—slides, podcast-only, slide + podcast, and video—on knowledge outcomes and participant evaluations. Methods A four-arm quasi-experimental pre-test–post-test design was conducted among health-related vocational school students (pre-test n = 188; post-test n = 183). Participants were assigned based on academic programs; individual-level matching was not possible due to anonymous data collection. Group comparisons were performed using non-parametric tests (Kruskal–Wallis, Mann–Whitney U with Holm correction), and effect sizes were reported. Results Pre-test scores differed slightly (p = .027, ε 2 = .034). Post-test scores showed significant differences with a moderate effect (p < .001, ε 2 = .203). The slide + podcast group achieved the highest scores (g = 1.74), followed by the slide group (g = 1.04). Minimal changes were observed in the podcast-only (g = 0.14) and video groups (g = 0.11). These g values reflect independent-sample differences rather than within-person change. Training evaluation scores differed (p < .001, ε 2 = .113), with higher ratings in multimodal formats but no difference between them. Conclusions Instructional format is associated with learning outcomes in risk assessment training. Multimodal approaches may better support learning in conceptually complex OHS content; however, findings should be interpreted as a pedagogical pattern rather than causal superiority.

items.title: Efficient Privacy-Preserving High-Dimensional Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
items.abstract: In the AI era, approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search on vector databases is critical as it supports similarity retrieval over high-dimensional vectors, which is essential for many large language model (LLM) applications. To reduce costs and improve scalability, vector databases are often outsourced to cloud servers, raising privacy concerns for users whose query vectors contain sensitive information. In this work, we study the problem of asymmetric privacy-preserving ANN search, where the vector database is public but user queries must remain private from an untrusted cloud server. To solve this problem, we propose ObliSC, an efficient privacy-preserving search framework that protects query privacy against access-pattern leakage. ObliSC consists of (i) a search base that retrieves ANNs with a strong privacy guarantee of full obliviousness; and (ii) parallel optimization strategies that accelerate candidate retrieval and refinement while preserving full obliviousness and retrieval quality. Experiments on six standard ANN benchmarks show that ObliSC not only achieves efficiency and result quality competitive with baseline methods but also maintains a lightweight index compared with the evaluated privacy-preserving approaches.

items.title: EgoCaptioner: Towards Comprehensive and Fine-Grained Egocentric Video Captioning
items.abstract: Egocentric video captioning requires fine-grained detail and accurate timing, yet current multimodal large language models (MLLMs) often miss brief actions, confuse their order, or misinterpret the wearer's motion. Existing caption formats also offer limited support for combining detailed narration with precise timing. We present EgoCaptioner, which pairs a video-level overview of the setting, participants, and the wearer's overall activity with timed steps whose narration adapts to varying perceptual demands and marks key moments at specific timestamps. We develop a coarse-to-fine annotation pipeline that establishes event structure before expanding step descriptions, yielding 50,000 training examples from eight egocentric video sources. Complementary rewards assess factual accuracy and coverage, measure step-level temporal alignment, and penalize fragmented or redundant narration, guiding caption refinement through Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). To improve the reliability of factual supervision, we supplement caption references with pose-derived motion facts when sensor data are available. Across five egocentric benchmarks, EgoCaptioner achieves leading performance among evaluated open-source models in caption quality, caption-conditioned question answering, and temporal alignment. It also surpasses Gemini 3.1 Pro on PhysCapBench and all evaluated proprietary baselines on Minerva-Ego under the caption-to-QA protocol. Ablations support the complementary roles of factual and temporal rewards and show that coarse-to-fine annotation provides more effective supervision than single-pass annotation.

items.abstract: This article examines the preservation, institutionalization, and opening up of documentary heritage relating to human rights violations committed during and in connection with Uruguay's last period of dictatorship (1968–2004). Taking the discovery of the Berrutti Archive in 2006 as its starting point, the article examines the transition from repressive secrecy to the establishment of a normative and institutional framework shaped by international standards and the demands of transitional justice. It also assesses interdisciplinary initiatives undertaken at the Universidad de la República, with particular emphasis on the data cross-referencing methodology developed by Proyecto Cruzar and the citizen science platform LUISA. Finally, the article addresses the developments and ethical and methodological dilemmas arising from the application of artificial intelligence, multimodal models, and knowledge graphs to degraded collections of repressive documentation. It concludes that the integration of archival rigor, technological innovation, and community participation is indispensable for consolidating the right to truth, collective memory, and guarantees of non-repetition.

items.title: EMERGING TECHNOLOGIES AND SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN NIGERIA: CHALLENGES FOR DIGITAL LEARNING SYSTEMS
items.abstract: The emergence of digital technologies, without doubt has continued to reshape educational systems across the globe, creating new opportunities for sustainable development in developing countries such as Nigeria. This study examines the nexus between emerging technologies and sustainable development with particular emphasis on digital learning systems in Nigeria. The increasing adoption of artificial intelligence, cloud computing, virtual learning platforms, mobile technologies, and digital communication tools has significantly transformed teaching, learning and knowledge dissemination in educational institutions. Despite these advancements, challenges such as inadequate technological infrastructure, poor internet connectivity, digital inequality, limited technical skills and inconsistent policy implementation has continued to undermine the effectiveness of digital learning systems in Nigeria. The paper adopts qualitative approach and makes use of secondary sources of data to bridge the gap in knowledge. The study examines the role of emerging technologies in promoting sustainable digital learning systems in Nigeria, identify the challenges associated with the adoption of digital learning technologies in educational institutions; and investigate the challenges affecting the effective integration of emerging technologies into Nigeria's educational system. The paper hinges on the Technology Acceptance Model and Diffusion of Innovation Theory as its theoretical frameworks. While Technology Acceptance Model explains users' acceptance and utilization of digital technologies based on perceived usefulness and ease of use. The diffusion of Innovation Theory provides insight into how technological innovations spread are adopted within educational and social systems. The paper concludes that although emerging technologies possess significant potential for transforming Nigeria's educational landscape and advancing sustainable development, deliberate investments in infrastructure, digital literacy, and supportive policies are necessary for achieving long-term effectiveness and inclusiveness

items.title: Enhancing Understanding of Language Models with Varied Explanations
items.abstract: Language models are increasingly used to support human judgement in complex reasoning tasks, yet their predictions often remain difficult to interpret and validate. Explainability techniques provide insight into model decision-making, helping expose errors, failure modes, and potential bias so users can decide whether to rely on model outputs. Explanations are simplified approximations of a language model's internal workings. The goal is to obtain explanations that reflect the underlying computation as closely as possible (faithfulness), are understandable to users (plausibility), and help them achieve their intended goals (utility). Evaluation protocols are essential for assessing these dimensions. This thesis studies highlight explanations, natural language explanations, and chain-of-thought reasoning. These forms offer complementary perspectives on model behaviour and exhibit distinct strengths and limitations across tasks. Producing explanations that satisfy multiple quality dimensions remains challenging, as does evaluating them reliably across forms and settings. This thesis aims to improve people's understanding of models' decision-making processes in complex reasoning tasks. First, it proposes two evaluation frameworks for assessing highlight explanations across multiple properties and explanation types, together with a meta-evaluation framework for examining the reliability of existing faithfulness metrics for chain-of-thought explanations. Second, it proposes two techniques that generate natural language explanations designed to be faithful to the model's prediction process while remaining concise, coherent, and helpful for understanding model decisions. Finally, a study of human-AI interaction explores the roles of evidence and explanations in helping users validate model verdicts in a fact-checking setting.

items.title: Ethical considerations in AI-enabled electrocardiography: a narrative review
items.abstract: Introduction Artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled electrocardiography (ECG) can detect arrhythmias, structural abnormalities, and physiological patterns not readily apparent through conventional interpretation. However, its rapid clinical integration raises ethical concerns. This review critically synthesizes literature on bias and fairness, privacy and confidentiality, explainability and transparency, clinical trust and automation bias, and governance and accountability. Methods We conducted a narrative review using structured searches of PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science. Review preparation was informed by the SANRA quality-assessment scale, and study selection was summarized using a flow diagram adapted from PRISMA-ScR (435 records identified; 46 studies included). Studies were eligible if they substantively examined ethical considerations in AI-ECG; those addressing technical performance alone were excluded. Evidence was classified by study design and clinical maturity. Results Ethical risks arose throughout the AI-ECG lifecycle, beyond the algorithm itself. Studies documented performance disparities across sex, age, race, and ethnicity, alongside vulnerabilities involving membership inference, biometric re-identification, and unintended attribute inference. Explainability remained inadequately evaluated, while automation bias raised concerns about clinical decision-making and patient safety. Governance and post-deployment oversight remained fragmented. Most quantitative evidence came from retrospective or experimental proof-of-concept studies rather than externally validated or clinically deployed systems. Discussion Responsible AI-ECG implementation requires a lifecycle approach addressing upstream bias, privacy safeguards, clinically meaningful explanations, clinician oversight, and post-deployment surveillance. We propose Inherent Protocol Bias (IPB) as an organizing framework linking downstream ethical risks to decisions in study design, data collection, validation, and deployment. Unlike dataset bias, selection bias, spectrum bias, measurement bias, and cohort-origin confounding, which describe specific sources or manifestations of error, IPB emphasizes the protocol-level decisions through which established biases arise or persist. IPB is not a new statistical form of bias but a framework for identifying actionable intervention points. We outline potential applications for improving fairness, privacy, accountability, and clinical trust; however, these recommendations remain conceptual and require empirical evaluation.

items.title: Ethical Dilemmas of AI Use in PAI Learning: A Teacher's Perception and Grade X Students' Learning Behaviors at MA As Syakur
items.abstract: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in Islamic Religious Education (IRE) offers opportunities to enhance students’ understanding but also raises ethical concerns regarding academic honesty and the accuracy of religious information. This study aims to analyze AI use, teacher perceptions, students’ learning behaviors, and the ethical dilemmas arising at MA As Syakur. Employing a descriptive qualitative approach, the study involved one IRE teacher and eight Grade X students selected purposively. Data were collected through interviews, classroom observations, and documentation of 33 student assignment books, then analyzed thematically. The findings reveal five patterns of AI use, ranging from seeking explanations and comparing information to directly copying AI-generated answers. Four of the eight student informants were found to have copied AI-generated answers into their assignment books. The teacher demonstrated an open yet cautious attitude, emphasizing the importance of guidance and information verification. This study highlights the need to promote AI literacy, academic honesty, and Islamic ethical values, particularly amanah (trustworthiness) and tabayyun (careful verification), in IRE learning. Future research should involve more madrasahs and employ longitudinal observations.

items.title: Ethical Dimensions of Computational Social Science Research: A Primer
items.abstract: This primer discusses the ethical questions raised by computational social science (CSS), that is, research that analyses data generated at scale by digital platforms, networked devices, and public administrations. Much of the ethical guidance available to CSS researchers was developed for clinical and interventional research, and it assumes a bounded study, an identifiable participant, and an occasion on which consent can be sought. Since much CSS research lacks these features, the primer examines where this guidance fits and where it does not. The primer is organised around six themes: data, privacy, and power; bias and equity; conceptual clarity and value-laden choices; stakeholder impact, justice, and participatory research; ethical communication and public engagement; and the use of generative AI in the research process. Each theme is introduced conceptually, illustrated with cases from the published literature, and followed by reflection questions that researchers can ask of their own projects. The primer is intended for researchers, research ethics committees, and teaching. It pays particular attention to research on administrative registers, including data held by Statistics Netherlands. The research for this publication was partly funded by ODISSEI, the Dutch national research infrastructure for the social sciences.

items.title: Evaluating the Ethical and Clinical Reliability of Large Language Models in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
items.abstract: Background Large language models (LLMs) are becoming a subject of great interest as a clinical decision-support tool, but their reliability is not well described in the surgical field of oral and maxillofacial surgery (OMFS). Objective This study aim ed to assess three popular general- purpose LLMs in the context of clinical accuracy, ethical safety, and risk awareness in 10 high-stakes OMFS scenarios. Methods Standardized clinical scenarios for postoperative emergencies, implant planning, trauma, oncology, and therapeutic management were used to prompt GPT-4, Claude 3, and Gemini. The responses were evaluated independently by two OMFS board-certified surgeons on an ordinal scale of 0–2 in three areas: clinical accuracy, ethical safety, and risk awareness. Mean scores were calculated and non-parametric comparisons were made. Results All models demonstrated high clinical accuracy (mean ± SD: GPT-4: 1.85 ± 0.42; Claude 3: 1.90 ± 0.38; Gemini: 1.75 ± 0.48), but exhibited significant variability in ethical safety (Claude 3: 1.75 ± 0.45; GPT-4: 1.60 ± 0.58; Gemini: 1.50 ± 0.52; Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.004). The risk awareness scores ranged between moderate (1.65–1.80) across models. The post hoc tests showed that the ethical safety scores differed significantly between Claude 3 and Gemini (Dunn's test, p = 0.008). Conclusions Although LLMs can provide guideline-concordant recommendations, inconsistent ethical framing and lack of escalation process directions restrict safe implementation of LLM in OMFS. A human in the loop structure and the ethics tuning pertaining to the domain are necessary prior to clinical integration. Clinical Relevance: While LLMs can offer prompt, clinically appropriate information in concert with guidelines, there is a great risk of overlooking the necessity to escalate to a specialist case in OMFS. These tools should be used as a complementary support tool in a well-defined framework of human-in-the-loop, until domain-specific ethical tuning and real-world validation are attained. Thus, clinical decision-making and patient safety are well protected under the authority of a qualified surgeon.

items.title: Evaluation of vibration transmissibility and ergonomic usability of anti-vibration gloves at real workstations
items.abstract: Exposure to hand transmitted vibration is common in workplaces using hand held-tools and contributes to upper limb disorders, including hand-arm vibration syndrome. Anti-vibration gloves are often the only personal protective equipment available, but their use remains limited because of discomfort and reduced manual dexterity, so glove assessment should extend beyond laboratory testing to real working conditions. This article proposes an extension of ISO 10819 based on eight vibration transmission coefficients determined in situ, together with comfort-related parameters such as dexterity and the force required to bend the fingers. The method was applied at four workstations differing in vibration characteristics, using an ISO 10819-compliant glove of a new design as a case study. Frequency-weighted exposure was reduced by 10–56% depending on the workstation, although at one workstation the results indicated amplification in one of the analysed axes. Compliance with ISO 10819 therefore does not guarantee protection at every workstation.

items.title: EvoCausalTwin: Drift-Aware Causal Structure Learning, Evidence-Calibrated Verification, and Budget-Constrained Intervention for Evolving Systems
items.abstract: Evolving systems undergo distributional, mechanistic, and structural changes that can invalidate static causal models and lead to poorly justified interventions. This paper presents EvoCausalTwin, an evidence-gated artificial intelligence framework linking dynamic causal structure learning, causal-drift decomposition, evidence-calibrated verification, budget-aware intervention, causal-effect decision analysis, and constrained workflow auditing. Its three language-model auditor roles share one quantized Llama3.1-8B-Instruct model and cannot orient graph edges or bypass statistical verification. We evaluate the framework on EvoCausalBench, comprising 2,000 source structural causal models and 50,000 episodes across four graph families, five mechanism families, five drift regimes, and 10–100 variables. Splits are assigned at the source-SCM level before episode generation. On the principal test set, EvoCausalTwin obtains SHD 4.8, directed F1 0.79, ATE RMSE 0.22, PEHE 0.32, five-class drift macro-F1 0.77, decision regret 0.24, and drift-class ECE 0.061, compared with 6.1, 0.74, 0.27, 0.39, 0.66, 0.36, and 0.142 for CD-NOD. Paired analysis uses 300 held-out SCM-level vectors. A separate 50,000-observation reliability audit yields decision-confidence weighted ECE 0.01845, with subgroup calibration reported across all five drift regimes. A full 2^4 factorial ablation distinguishes the descriptive contributions of modules M2–M5. Twelve-month operational evidence is retrospective and does not establish prospective causal treatment effectiveness. The findings support a framework-level contribution under the evaluated protocols, not a new standalone causal-discovery estimator
